title: Non-Hermetic Builds
damaged_code:
```bash
# Makefile
# Depends on whatever arbitrary compiler version happens to exist on the host OS
build:
	gcc main.c -o app
```
pattern: Compiling application code using the host operating system's system-installed compilers, tools, or global environment libraries.
why_bad: Results in non-reproducible builds. Compile behavior will vary silently across developer workstations and CI agents, introducing subtle performance drifts or ABI mismatch crashes in production.
detection: Build scripts executing global binary paths (such as raw `gcc` or `rustc`) without pinned toolchains or cryptographic hash manifests for tools.
counterexample:
```toml
# rust-toolchain.toml
[toolchain]
channel = "1.72.0" # Statically lock the compiler toolchain version
```
fix: Statically declare all compilation toolchain versions, libraries, and dependencies in project files, ensuring builds run inside hermetic environments like Bazel or Docker.
source: Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 14.
